result.title: Task presentation and execution paths shape LLM mathematical performance
result.summary: Mathematical performance depends on how a language model receives information, uses generated text and submits an answer. We study these dependencies through paired comparisons that separate submission requirements, draft reuse and candidate availability. On 65 development problems, an instruction permitting continued derivation produced no valid final answers in 390 short-output calls; a single-line submission instruction produced 390 format-valid outputs, including 389 parseable answers. Under the fixed submission protocol, 198 problems with failed initial submissions were answered correctly in 9.09p of cases with the question alone, 33.84p with its draft, 46.46p with candidates, and 59.60p with both. Drafts added 13.13 percentage points with candidates fixed, and candidates added 25.76 points with drafts fixed; both effects were significant after Holm correction and were subadditive on the accuracy scale. Retaining a trailing excerpt outperformed retaining a leading excerpt of similar average length by 10.10 points Holm-adjusted p 0.027. A second completion model showed the same directions of input effects on the fixed materials. In a cohort with parseable initial submissions, candidates added no correct answers when the previous draft was supplied, but added 27 points when it was absent. These results establish a conditional value of generated text: a failed submission can leave useful material, whose contribution depends on what else is supplied and what is retained.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文用配对比较考察数学任务中提交格式、草稿复用、候选答案可得性及保留片段位置如何影响 LLM 的最终正确率，并报告各因素的条件性贡献。
AI.relevance_reason: 其固定材料、分离「草稿」与「候选」贡献的实验范式，可供核查 LVR 中生成状态是否被答案实际使用及贡献分配；但属纯文本提示效应，与视觉状态和 latent 表示的关联需进一步判断。
